title: Hybrid kernel-path admission smoother for continuous batching and tail-latency mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are implementing a Hybrid Kernel-Path Admission Smoother (HKPAS) that bridges admission control decisions with kernel-selection heuristics to reduce 95th/99th token latency during continuous batching workloads (prefill+decode). This ticket covers design, implementation, benchmarks, rollout, and monitoring for the initial HKPAS prototype.

Background: Current admission decisions are largely size/age and slot-based; kernel selection is orthogonal. For many workloads (heterogeneous sequence lengths + mixed model variants) suboptimal kernel-path choices at admission time and abrupt batch-shape changes cause tail spikes during prefill->decode transitions. Prior work (ENG-8421 and ENG-31247) improved admission heuristics and opportunistic prefill, but we still see 95p token latency regressions during bursty traffic and transient microbursts.

Goals:
- Reduce 95th and 99th token latency by 15-30% for mixed-short/long workloads without sacrificing overall throughput.
- Avoid oscillatory kernel handovers under transient load.
- Integrate with kernel probing logic so admission decisions account for probable kernel path and its latency characteristics.
- Provide safe rollout with canary, rollback, and metrics-driven automatic fallback.

Design overview (HKPAS):
- Admission-time kernel affinity scoring: When a request is admitted, compute a small vector of likelihoods for preferred kernel paths (e.g., attention-optimised kernel A, quantized kernel Q, fused-attention kernel F) based on request features (sequence length, model variant, temperature, expected decode length). Score is a lightweight estimator learned from historical traces (logistic model stored as small table) that runs in ~100ns.
- Latency budget tokens: Requests carry a per-request latency budget computed from route SLO and current headroom. Admission gates prefer placements that preserve cumulative budget while maximizing batch coalescence.
- Slot salting & soft-reservation: To avoid abrupt batch-shape changes, HKPAS salts a fraction of slots with low-priority “soft-reservations” that accept compatible kernel paths; these slots are prefilled opportunistically and can be reclaimed for latency-critical traffic.
- Kernel-aware backpressure: If kernel-probe indicates high variance for a kernel path (recent tail events), admission throttle down assignments to that kernel path and steer new prefills to alternate kernels or slower-but-stable paths.
- Proactive kernel probing: lightweight probing jobs periodically run short synthetic prefill+decode sequences to update kernel-affinity scores and tail variance estimates.

Implementation plan:
1) Data collection & feature extractor (MVP): extend admission metadata to include sequence-length histogram, model-variant tag, and predicted decode length. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892)
2) Kernel affinity estimator service (in-runtine small module): implement table-based estimator + periodic updater reading probe results.
3) Admission smoother logic integrated into the admission controller and prefill coordinator.
4) Soft-slot salting mechanism and reclaim path.
5) Monitoring & alarms: new dashboards and SLO checks for kernel-path distribution, 95/99 token latency, slot-reclamation rates.

Success metrics (canary):
- 95p token latency <= previous 95p * 0.85 on mixed workload synthetic benchmark.
- 99p token latency improvement of at least 10% for initial canary traffic.
- No decrease in tokens/sec beyond 5% across the canary group.

Benchmark plan and datasets:
- Synthetic mix A: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 20% medium (128-256), 10% long (>=512) decoding, spike patterns: Poisson bursts and deterministic microbursts.
- Real-customer replay from anonymized traces (two customers) across different model variants.

Rollout plan:
- Local dev and unit tests (week 1)
- Integration test in staging with synthetic mixes (week 2)
- Canary on 5% of serving capacity for 48 hours with automated rollback on SLO regressions (week 3)
- Gradual ramp to 50% over 1 week; full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Observability & runbook:
- Dashboards: kernel-path heatmap, admission decision breakdown, slot salting occupancy, 95/99 token latency per model and per kernel-path.
- Alerts: 95p increase >10% over baseline for >5 minutes; kernel-probe failure rate >1%; slot-reclamation surge >20%.
- Runbook actions: Force-fallback to legacy admission strategy, disable slot-salting, quarantine unstable kernel paths.

Open questions & risks:
- Estimator cold-start: mitigated via seeded priors from offline traces; probe frequency tuned to avoid noise.
- Interference with autoscaling: kernel steering may concentrate work on specific GPUs; need to coordinate with scheduler constraints.
- Complexity & maintainability: HKPAS introduces heuristics; we will keep estimator lightweight and document the rules in Confluence.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/HKPAS+Design
- PR (MVP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892
- Benchmark dashboard (staging): https://dd.redwood.ai/dashboard/runtime/hkpas-canary

Next steps:
- Finish data collection instrumentation and landing PR-1892 (owned by Marco)
- Implement estimator + probe harness (owner: Marco)
- Add unit/integration tests and staging job (owner: Aisha)
